newsitem.title: USA: Political parties campaign contributions reported.
newsitem.headline: Political parties campaign contributions reported.

text.p: National Republican and Democratic party committees poured at least $38.6 million into election campaigns for president and control of Congress, the Federal Election Commission reported on Tuesday.

It said the Democratic National Committee contributed $2.8 million and the Republican National Committee contributed $19.2 million, but did not say how much of that went to President Bill Clinton and Republican challenger Bob Dole.

The commission said all the contributions were for the 21 months from Jan. 1, 1995, to Oct. 16, except for the Democratic National Committee, which sparked a controversy by initially refusing to report contributions and expenditures for the first two weeks of October.
Republican Party chairman Haley Barbour implied the Democrats were trying to hide contributions.

Sen. Christopher Dodd, general chairman of the Democratic National Committee, issued a statement saying its staff believed no report was legally required because the committee made no contributions during the two weeks, but said the committee decided to file the report.
For Senate campaigns, the election commission said the Democratic Senatorial Committee contributed $6.4 million and the National Republican Senatorial Committee contributed $1.4 million.
For House of Representatives races, it said the National Republican Congressional Committee contributed $4.2 million and the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee contributed $4.6 million.

But the commission said the $38.6 million was only the amount contributed under federal election law limits. It listed other money not subject to the limits, including $4.4 million in "independent expenditure" contributions by the Republican Senate committee.

The commission also said both political parties have raised and spent record amounts of so-called "soft money." The money is not supposed to be used for federal campaigns but organisations including the citizens lobby Common Cause have said some of it is used indirectly to support federal candidates.
The commission said Republican parties raised $121 million in "soft money" and spent $118 million of it. It said Democratic parties raised $102 million and spent $93 million.
